x-fc-pending.title: Pending of the spec
x-fc-pending.description: Corrections to the shapes of the operations and events of spec/funnelchat.json (the spec the developers portal publishes) where production answers otherwise: fields, query parameters, responses and the type of some events. The generator (`composer generate`, scripts/generate.php) applies each one before generating the resources and types, only while the snapshot still has the shape it corrects: when a new snapshot changes it, generation uses the snapshot's version and reports which entries in this file can be deleted. This layer never adds an operation or an event: the SDK has only what the portal publishes, and an entry for a route or an event the snapshot lacks is left out and reported. Every entry comes from the code of the tags running in production (`origin` and `sources` say which).

rules.paths: Not applied: the SDK has only the operations the snapshot publishes. A route here is reported as obsolete when the snapshot has it, and as not published (left out) when it does not; either way it can be deleted.
rules.operationPatches: A patch adds properties to the body of a snapshot operation only while that operation meets the `while` condition.
rules.webhooks: An event replaces the snapshot's while it meets the `x-fc-replace-while` condition. An event the snapshot does not publish is not added (it is reported).
rules.responsePatches: A patch replaces the responses of a snapshot operation (all the 2xx ones, and any others it includes by code) only while that operation meets the `while` condition.
rules.webhookPatches: A patch adds properties to the `data` of an event (of every event with `type: "*"`) only while the event does not include them (neither in its schema nor in its example); `required` makes them required in the type.
rules.components.schemas: The schemas in this layer start with `Pending` so they do not clash with the snapshot's.
rules.schemaPatches: A patch adds properties to a snapshot schema only while the schema does not include them.
rules.parameterPatches: A patch adds query parameters to a snapshot operation only while that operation does not declare them.
rules.conditions: `while` and `x-fc-replace-while` take top-level keys of the snapshot's operation or event, or JSON pointers into it (`/responses/200/content/application~1json/schema/type`), where `null` means absent or null: a correction stops by itself, and is reported as obsolete, once the snapshot changes the very thing it corrects.

x-fc-pending.origin: Reviewed on 22-10 against the code of the versions in production that day: conversations v1.18.10, communities v2.34.52, accounts v1.4.24, the API entrypoint (api-edge) v0.3.0 and platform-gate v0.8.0. It started from the Node SDK's pending layer; the accounts webhook entries of 16-10 were reviewed against v1.4.24. Reviewed again on 04-11 against the versions in production that day: accounts v1.5.97, conversations v1.19.7, communities v2.35.5, platform-gate v0.9.1 and the API entrypoint deployed on 25-10, which also routes `/connect-links` and `/connect`. What changed for the first use (connecting a number, sending, knowing when it was read, receiving, groups and workspaces): the numbers by API now come from accounts, sending to a group and reading its action are in, the participant events say that `campaign` can be `null`, and every event carries `data.workspace_id`. Phase 2, the same day: the snapshot became the portal's full unified spec (portal v0.6.0), made of accounts v1.5.97, conversations v1.19.7 and communities v2.35.5. What it brings was deleted from here. What stays is what it lacks (the forms routes, rotate-secret, sending to a group, the events accounts delivers that are not in its `webhooks`, `data.workspace_id`) and corrections where its shapes, inferred from the code, are not what production answers; each correction carries the condition that ends it. Phase 3, 05-11: the full spec of portal v0.6.2, with conversations v1.19.21 (sending by phone) and sending to a group: sending to a group is now in the snapshot. Phase 4, 05-11: the full spec of portal v0.6.3, with communities v2.35.7: following a group (`POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/import`) comes from the snapshot, nothing new here. Phase 5, 11-11: the snapshot is the spec the developers portal publishes (https://developers-portal.funnelchat.app/specs/funnelchat.json), no longer its full unified spec, by decision of 11-11: the SDK has only what the portal publishes, and this layer no longer adds anything (the generator leaves out and reports a route or an event the snapshot lacks). First v0.6.12 (sha256 f8baa487…, 241 operations), then v0.6.13 (sha256 a7b48074…, 253 operations and 56 event types; it adds `GET /me`, the alerts, the details of a flow, the result by group of a scheduled send and the category of each group). The forms routes are the snapshot's: deleted from here. `rotate-secret` and the events `billing.plan_blocked`, `subscription.expiring` and `ai_quota.*` are not published: deleted, with the schemas only they used. The events accounts delivers (`device.*`, billing, subscription, MAC, `account.blocked`, `group_action.*`, `daily_report.generated`, `campaign.no_groups_available`, `group.full`, `group.message_received`, `group.reaction_added`, `group_join_request.*`) are in the snapshot, but typed only by an example (three without one: `billing.payment_failed`, `billing.upcoming_charge`, `subscription.dormant_ending`), which loses what can be `null` and the values of `reason`, `state` and `identity_type`. So they stay here, typed from production, as corrections with `x-fc-replace-while` (while the snapshot's `data` has no schema), like the five of conversations and communities. For `group.message_received` and `group.reaction_added` the example of v0.6.13 said `message.id` where production sends `message.uid` (communities v2.35.28, in production, checked on 11-11). Every other correction stays too: the published spec still has the shapes they correct (the four sends, the QR, a link read, the revoke and the delete, `webhooks->update()`, the two listings, an action read, the query parameters and `data.workspace_id`). Phase 6, 13-11: v0.6.14 (sha256 37c54a5a…), the same 253 operations and 56 event types. The only change is the example of `group.message_received` and `group.reaction_added`, which now shows `message.uid`, as production sends it; their `data` still has no schema, so those two are corrected like the other events accounts delivers: while the snapshot's `data` has no schema (until 13-11 their condition was that the example lacked `message.uid`, which v0.6.14 would have ended, leaving them typed only by an example). Checked on 13-11 against the code of the services that send them: `group_join_request.*` always carries `participant.identity` (without one the event does not go out) and its `identity_type` is `phone` or `whatsapp_user`; `answers[].label` of `whatsapp_form.completed` is always a string (the question's name when it has no label); and `message.type` of `message.received` can take values the spec does not list yet, so the type accepts any string besides the known ones.

sources.accounts-webhooks: accounts v1.4.24, checked again against v1.5.97 (in production on 04-11): the same routes and shapes; since workspaces, a key sees, counts and changes only the subscriptions of its workspace, and the limit of 50 is per workspace. With an API key: permissions `webhooks:read` / `webhooks:write` (the `GET /api/v1/webhooks/events` catalog requires `accounts:read`); the list and the history are paginated; `rotate-secret` is not open to API keys (403 route_not_available). What stays here: the query parameters production accepts and the spec lacks (`perPage` of the list; `per_page`, `event_type` and `event_id` of the history) and the answer of `PUT`, which the spec types as an empty object.
sources.communities-participant-events: communities v2.35.5 (in production on 04-11): `campaign` is `null` for a group without a campaign, and the event goes out for any group of the account, not only campaign ones; `identity_type` is `phone` or `whatsapp_user`. accounts v1.5.97 delivers them (`active` in its catalog).
sources.communities-group-messages: communities v2.35.5 (in production on 04-11): sending a message to a group and reading how it ended, open to API keys in production since 04-11, and the events `group_action.completed` and `group_action.failed`. The full spec of 05-11 brings both routes; what stays here is the answer of reading an action, which it types as a list (production answers an object), and the two events.
sources.communities-events: communities v2.34.52, unchanged in v2.35.5 (except the workspace, which travels to accounts apart): `group.message_received`, `group.reaction_added` and `group_join_request.*`; accounts delivers them (all `active` in its catalog). Checked again on 11-11 against communities v2.35.28 (in production): `group.message_received` and `group.reaction_added` carry `message.uid`; the published spec's example said `message.id` up to v0.6.13 and shows `message.uid` since v0.6.14. Checked again on 13-11: `group_join_request.*` is not sent without `participant.identity`, so it is never `null`, and `identity_type` is `phone` or `whatsapp_user`, never `unknown`. All four are corrected while the snapshot's `data` has no schema.
sources.conversations-send: conversations v1.18.10 (in production since 21-10): sends made with an API key respond 200 with the message queued (the 13-10 snapshot still said 204), with the message, its status, the forward results, the file types, `client_reference` and the refusals. Checked again against v1.19.7 (in production on 04-11): the same answers; the routes now act in the key's workspace. The full spec of 04-11 types `message` as nullable: for an API key it never is, so the four sends keep `message` required here.
sources.conversations-listings: conversations v1.19.7 (in production on 04-11): listing the templates answers template resources, and listing the contacts of a tag answers contact resources; the full spec types their items as `object` and as `string`.
sources.conversations-events: conversations v1.18.10: the 15 `live` event types and the payloads of `message.status_changed`, `message.received` and `whatsapp_form.completed`, the same in v1.19.7 (in production on 04-11). The full spec of 04-11 types these events only by an example (every id an `int`, `error` and `client_reference` always there, `answers[].value` a string): they stay typed from production here while it does. Checked again on 13-11: `answers[].label` is always a string (the question's name when it has no label) and `answers[].value` can be `null`; `message.type` of `message.received` has the values of the spec's enum, but new ones can appear, so it is typed as those values or any other string.
sources.accounts-workspace-id: accounts v1.5.97 (in production on 04-11): every event it delivers carries `data.workspace_id`, the workspace the event is routed to (an integer, or `null`): its own events, the ones conversations and communities relay, and `webhook.test`; its catalog puts it in every example. platform-gate v0.9.1 lets `workspace_id` through in `data`.
sources.accounts-number-onboarding: accounts v1.5.97 (in production on 04-11): `POST /api/v1/devices`, `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/qr` (`expires_in` 5 with a QR), the `external_reference` filter of `GET /api/v1/devices`, the `connect-links` routes (`503 meta_connect_disabled` while the Meta sign-up by link is off), the `Idempotency-Key` header of both creates, `external_reference` and `connection` on the number, and the events `device.connected` (with `connection`, `external_reference` and `connect_link_id`), `device.disconnected` (with `reason`), `device.deleted` and `device.health_changed`, which always carry `device.connection`, `device.external_reference` and `connect_link_id`. They match accounts' own OpenAPI of 26-10. Since workspaces, the numbers and the links a key sees and creates are those of its workspace. What stays here corrects the spec: the QR answer (always `{data}`), a link read (`url` always there and `null`), the revoke and the delete of a number (an empty body), and `perPage` of the links list.

PendingWebhookSubscription.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingWebhookSubscription` keeps working: since the full spec of 04-11 it is the snapshot's `WebhookSubscriptionResource`.

PendingWebhookSubscriptionCreate.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingWebhookSubscriptionCreate` keeps working: since the full spec of 04-11 it is the snapshot's `StoreWebhookSubscriptionRequest`.

PendingWebhookSubscriptionUpdate.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingWebhookSubscriptionUpdate` keeps working: the snapshot's `UpdateWebhookSubscriptionRequest`.

PendingWebhookSubscriptionDelivery.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingWebhookSubscriptionDelivery` keeps working: since the full spec of 04-11 it is the snapshot's `WebhookSubscriptionDeliveryResource`.

PendingPublicMessage.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingPublicMessage` keeps working: since the full spec of 04-11 it is the snapshot's `PublicMessageResource`.

PendingMessageError.description: Why it failed. If Funnelchat decided it, `code` is `null`, `title` is a text and `reason` gives the reason; if WhatsApp reported it, `code` and `title` are Meta's and `reason` is `null`.

PendingExternalReference.description: Your own reference for the number (for example, your customer's ID). Free text, it can repeat. It comes back in the number, in the list filter and in every `device.*` event.

PendingDeviceCreate.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingDeviceCreate` keeps working: since the full spec of 04-11 it is the snapshot's `StoreDeviceRequest`.

qr_code.description: A PNG image as a data URI (`data:image/png;base64,…`), or `null` once the number is connected.

expires_in.description: Seconds before asking for the QR again: 5 with a QR (show it and scan it right away), 3 while the session starts, 0 once connected.

PendingConnectLinkErrorCode.description: Why the link did not complete, or `null`.

PendingConnectLinkCreate.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingConnectLinkCreate` keeps working: since the full spec of 04-11 it is the snapshot's `StoreConnectLinkRequest`.

PendingConnectLink.description: A single-use link where your customer creates or reconnects a number, without a Funnelchat session. A `meta` link tolerates retries: after a Facebook or Meta failure it stays `pending` so your customer can try again on the page, and the fifth failure makes it `failed` (`facebook_auth_failed` or `meta_error`); `quota_exceeded`, `trial_number_blocked` and `number_not_owned` close it at the first attempt.

url.description: `https://<public host>/connect/<token>` in the answer of the create; `null` when you read the link (the token is not stored).

device_id.description: The number to reconnect, or the one it created once `completed`; `null` otherwise.

country.description: The country given when creating the link, or `null`.

PendingWorkspaceId.description: The workspace of the event: the one it was routed to, which is the workspace of every subscription that receives it (a subscription receives only the events of its workspace: the one of the API key that created it, or the one chosen in the panel). An account with a single workspace gets the id of its default workspace. `null` only for an account without any workspace.

uid.description: The group's WhatsApp id (`…@g.us`): the `{group}` of `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/messages`.

identity.description: The phone, or the WhatsApp id (`…@lid`) when there is no phone.

PendingGroupMessageCreate.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingGroupMessageCreate` keeps working: since the full spec of 05-11 it is the snapshot's `SendGroupMessageRequest`.

PendingGroupActionAccepted.description: Kept so `@phpstan-import-type PendingGroupActionAccepted` keeps working: since the full spec of 05-11 it is the snapshot's `ApiGroupActionAcceptedResource`.

PendingGroupActionResult.description: It depends on the action. Sending a message: `message.uid`, the message's id in WhatsApp. Creating a group or renewing its link: `invite_link`. Actions with a list of phones: `participants`, one per person. The others: `{}`.

PendingGroupAction.description: An action on a group requested through the API, with its state and its result.

device_id.description: The number that runs it; `null` if it is no longer of the key's workspace.

PendingConnectLinkId.description: The connect link that connected this number the last time, or `null`. In `device.connected`, the link of that connection.

PendingConnectionType.description: How the number is connected: `qr` (WhatsApp Web session, not official), `coexistence` (WhatsApp Cloud API alongside the WhatsApp Business app), `dedicated` (WhatsApp Cloud API only), or `null` when it cannot be told.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Page size (25 by default, 100 at most), as every listing with an API key.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Page size (25 by default, 100 at most).

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Only the attempts of this event type.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Only the attempts of this event (`id` of the delivery).

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Page size (25 by default, 100 at most).

200.description: The registered message (`status: queued`), never `null` for an API key: production always answers `{"message": <object>}` (a message that could not be queued arrives as `failed` with `error.reason` `not_queued`; one that could not be registered is a `500`).
Always `{"data": …}`. The bare and string variants of the snapshot never reach the answer.
The links, paginated, newest first. `url` is always there and `null`: it carries the token, which is only in the answer of the create (ConnectLinkResource).
The link. `url` is always there and `null`: it carries the token, which is only in the answer of the create (ConnectLinkResource).
Empty body. The deletion is physical and frees the quota; it emits `device.deleted`.
The contacts with the tag, paginated: `ContactResource` items.

post.description: One of the account's numbers connected: when the QR code was scanned or when a WhatsApp Cloud number finished onboarding, also from a connect link. With `device.connection`, `device.external_reference` and `connect_link_id` (the link of this connection, or `null`).

One of the account's numbers disconnected and can no longer send or receive: a QR session closed or protected from a shadow ban, an official number left without registration, or disconnected in the panel. With `reason`, `device.connection`, `device.external_reference` and `connect_link_id` (the last link that connected the number, or `null`).

A number was deleted from the account (once per number, after the deletion, with the number as it was; `connect_link_id` is the last link that connected it, or `null`). The deletion is physical and frees the quota; an official number loses the app subscription but is not deregistered from Meta; a QR number's session is closed.

The aggregated health of an official number changed, according to Meta (not on every Meta webhook; `connect_link_id` is the last link that connected it, or `null`). The reason is read with `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/health`.
A subscription charge could not be processed (Stripe subscriptions only).
The next subscription charge is approaching (Stripe subscriptions only).
The trial period is about to end.
The scheduled cancellation of the subscription was reverted (Stripe subscriptions only).
The subscription cancellation was confirmed (Stripe subscriptions only).
The dormant account period is about to end.
The account reached 80 % of its monthly active contacts for the cycle.
The account used up its monthly active contacts for the cycle; a 24-hour grace period starts.
Some monthly active contacts expire in the next 7 days.
The account was blocked for usage: the 24-hour grace period after using up its monthly active contacts ended.

An action on a group failed as a whole. For an action requested through the API (a message sent to a group), `action.uuid` is the `action_id` of its `202` and `pipeline` is `null`; for one run by a campaign or a pipeline, `action.uuid` is `null`. `group` and `campaign` can be `null`.

uuid.description: The `action_id` of an action requested through the API.

type.description: `send_message` for a message sent to a group.

post.description: An action on a group requested through the API finished. `action.uuid` is the `action_id` of its `202` and `action.type` says which action it was; for a message sent to a group (`send_message`), `result.message.uid` is the message's id in WhatsApp. `group` and `campaign` can be `null`.
The account's daily report was generated (clicks, joins and exits).
A campaign has no groups to send the people who come in through its link to.
A group went from not full to full.
Someone wrote in a group of one of the account's numbers. It does not arrive for messages from your own numbers.

media_url.description: Files only; it can be `null` or a temporary URL.

identity.description: The phone, or the WhatsApp ID (`…@lid` or a BSUID) if there is no phone.

post.description: Someone reacted to a message in a group.

identity.description: The phone, or the WhatsApp ID (`…@lid` or a BSUID) if there is no phone.

post.description: Someone asked to join an official group.

identity.description: The phone, or the WhatsApp ID (`…@lid` or a BSUID) if there is no phone. Never `null`: without an identity the event does not go out.

post.description: Someone withdrew their request to join an official group.

identity.description: The phone, or the WhatsApp ID (`…@lid` or a BSUID) if there is no phone. Never `null`: without an identity the event does not go out.

post.description: The delivery status of a sent 1:1 message changed. One notice per transition, never one that goes backward; `queued` never arrives here. Request it by name in `events`: a subscription lists its types, with no wildcard.

message_id.description: The message's `id` in the contact's history.

device_id.description: The number on your account that sent the message.

client_reference.description: The `client_reference` you included in the send, or `null`.

post.description: Someone joined a WhatsApp group of the account, with or without a campaign: `campaign` is `null` when the group has none.
Someone left a WhatsApp group of the account (or was removed), with or without a campaign: `campaign` is `null` when the group has none.
A contact completed a WhatsApp form. It can arrive more than once: deduplicate by `id`.

label.description: Always a string: the question's name when it has no label.

value.description: Dates as ISO strings; texts up to 600 characters.

post.description: A contact wrote to one of the account's WhatsApp numbers. `device_id` is the number that received it: the same `device_id` you send with to answer from that number, `null` if the message has no number.

id.description: The message's `id` in the contact's history.

type.description: One of the known values, or a new one: the list can grow without a new version of the spec, so handle any other string too.

text.description: The text or the caption; `null` when there is none.

phone.description: Your number that received it, E.164.
